generated.text:
Summary
This update covers our penetration test status, data location and cross-border questions, DPA blockers, and retention by data type. Several items are still draft, reported or unconfirmed, and we have flagged them below.

Current position
The February 2026 external penetration test summary records no Critical or High findings. [C1] Two Medium findings (M-01 internal service-token scope and M-02 rate-limit bypass under a retry pattern) were open in the original report. [C2] Engineering reports the two Medium findings were remediated later; closure evidence is pending. [C3] The pen test summary we hold contains no remediation evidence. [C4]

A draft, proposed Acme configuration lists AWS ca-central-1 for supplier persistence; it is not proof of deployed state. [C5] That draft also proposes OpenAI as primary inference, with the Anthropic fallback intended to be off unless approved. [C6] Our internal notes say the Anthropic fallback for Acme would probably be disabled if residency or legal requires it, but this is not finalized. [C7]

Legal states the DPA is blocked until subprocessors and cross-border transfers are confirmed. [C8]

On retention, the draft proposes application logs of 14 days for Acme. [C9] Engineering reports enterprise app logs should be 14 days now, and a team member confirmed this for app logs only; observability traces have separate configuration. [C10] Source files currently persist for the workspace lifetime, and customer-specific retention is still to be determined. [C11] Observability payload capture is intended to be off in the draft. [C12]

Pending verification or evidence
We do not yet have retest or closure evidence for M-01 and M-02, and we hold only a summary rather than the full report, so we cannot state these findings as closed. Where OpenAI inference runs for the Acme configuration, and any other processing or fallback locations, is not yet confirmed; storage in Canada does not establish processing location. We have not completed a transfer analysis on whether content leaves Canada during processing. Whether the draft configuration is deployed is unconfirmed. The subprocessor list is not confirmed. We have no configuration reference for the 14-day app-log setting, and we have not yet stated retention for prompts, responses or observability traces. Acme-specific source-file retention is not yet set.

What we need from you
Please tell us whether the pilot will stay synthetic-only or include real customer-support transcripts, as this affects the retention and data-location answers. Please also tell us whether you require the Anthropic fallback to be disabled for Acme.

Next steps
We will ask Engineering for retest or closure evidence for M-01 and M-02, and for the full pen test report or an approved summary that can be shared. We will ask Engineering to confirm inference and processing locations and the deployed persistence region. We will ask Legal to confirm whether subprocessors and cross-border transfers are the only open DPA blockers. We will ask Engineering to confirm deployed app-log retention with a configuration reference and to state retention separately for traces, prompts, responses and source files. No dates are confirmed for any of these items yet.
